claims.text: Warm forging followed by a short annealing step will simultaneously increase strength and ductility relative to the as-cast condition in lamellar eutectic high-entropy alloys.
The simultaneous improvement from warm forging and annealing will be caused by refinement of lamellar spacing.
As-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 has a two-phase lamellar microstructure.
The lamellae in as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 are coarse.
The appropriate forging temperature is 700–900°C.
Forging should be followed by a brief anneal at approximately 900–1000°C.
Rapid cooling after annealing is part of the proposed effective treatment.
As-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 can display a fine-scale lamellar microstructure.
Thermomechanical treatment can produce refined lamellar or hierarchical microstructural features in AlCoCrFeNi2.1.
The proposed warm-forging treatment specifically increases the density of interphase boundaries.
Reduced lamellar spacing creates additional barriers to dislocation motion.
Additional barriers to dislocation motion increase strength.
Refined or hierarchical lamellar structures enhance strain accommodation.
The refined structure delays crack initiation or arrests microcracks, thereby improving ductility.
The treatment will increase yield strength by about 20% relative to the as-cast baseline.
The treatment will improve elongation by about 10% relative to the as-cast baseline.
The intervention is effective in EHEAs containing stable refractory or intermetallic lamellar phases.
Excessive forging temperature or annealing time can coarsen the microstructure and reduce the mechanical benefit.
The exact forging temperature, strain, and annealing parameters require composition-specific optimization.
Failure to reduce lamellar spacing or failure to improve both strength and ductility relative to an as-cast control would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The initial state and baseline characterize the as-cast lamellae as coarse, whereas the conditions describe the applicable as-cast materials as having fine-scale lamellae. The cited evidence also characterizes as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 as fine lamellar.
